title: P0 hosted api ephemeral proxy healthcheck loop - postmortem
summary: On 2029-09-03 between 02:12 and 03:07 UTC we experienced a P0 degradation of the Hosted API characterized by rising p50/p95/p99 request latency, a burst of 502/503 streaming failures, and partial streaming fragments that required client reconnects. Approximately 38% of active streaming sessions observed intermittent truncated chunks. The incident was traced to an emergent feedback loop where an internal ephemeral proxy fleet began performing aggressive healthchecks and connection resets that amplified client reconnect storms and overloaded the regional edge acceptors.
impact: Client-facing: Customers saw increased tail latency and up to 30% request error rates for streaming endpoints in us-west1 for a 55-minute window; non-stream (batch) endpoints had lower surface impact but experienced elevated p99s. Operational: ingress acceptor backlog grew, causing transient connection drops and partial responses that required client retries. Estimated customer sessions affected: ~14k. SLA impact: one minute breach of 99.9% for the region observed in billing metrics.
detection: Automated synthetic streaming probes raised an alert at 02:15 UTC for p99 TTFB > 2s. Streaming error rate alert (5xx > 5% over 5m) fired at 02:22 UTC. Pager duty pages went to SRE and Edge oncall simultaneously. Early on-call notes indicated repetitive proxy healthcheck logs and high connection churn on the edge proxies.
timeline: 02:12 UTC - first deviation in synthetic probes; 02:15 UTC - p99 TTFB alert; 02:18 UTC - edge metrics show spike in acceptor_queue length; 02:22 UTC - streaming 5xx alert fired; 02:25 UTC - oncall investigation finds healthcheck flapping from ephemeral-proxy-group-3; 02:34 UTC - temporary mitigation: scale-down of ephemeral-proxy-group-3 and increase keepalive timeout on edge; 02:40 UTC - client error rates begin to decline; 03:07 UTC - system metrics returned to baseline; 03:25 UTC - rollback of temporary config changes after monitoring; 09:00 UTC - post-incident trigger for follow-ups and root cause analysis.
technical_analysis: Root signal: a recently-deployed change to the ephemeral internal proxy fleet (proxy v3.2.1) introduced an aggressive healthcheck policy: probes were configured to mark upstreams unhealthy after 1 failed TCP keepalive and to immediately issue TCP resets to active connections when a healthcheck failed. Two compounding factors amplified impact: 1) our edge acceptor drain behavior interacted poorly with the proxy resets, leaving half-open streams on the edge which returned 502s to clients; 2) the client SDKs used exponential backoff disabled during ephemeral reconnection flows (override flag used by internal partner services), causing synchronized reconnect bursts. Analysis of logs shows healthcheck failure spikes correlated with an external load pattern (a partner test job that produced brief client bursts), which triggered the proxy policy to rapidly cycle upstreams. Kernel-level socket counts on edge nodes spiked, acceptor queues saturated, and scheduling stalls manifested as higher latencies.
root_cause: A combination of a too-aggressive healthcheck config in proxy v3.2.1 and a disabled reconnect backoff on some internal client SDKs. The proxy behavior (immediate TCP RST on healthcheck fail) is the proximate cause of partial streaming responses and 502s. The underlying enabler was a recent config change that was rolled to ephemeral-proxy-group-3 without automated canary safeguards for healthcheck aggressiveness.
immediate_mitigation: 1) Scaled down ephemeral-proxy-group-3 to reduce churn and moved traffic to stable proxy groups; 2) Increased edge acceptor keepalive and connection drain windows to allow graceful upstream failover; 3) Rolled back proxy healthcheck policy to previous threshold for the affected group; 4) Coordinated with partner services to re-enable SDK backoff flags and temporarily rate-limit their test job.
permanent_fixes: 1) Patch proxy to remove the immediate TCP RST-on-fail behavior and adopt half-open-safe draining with the existing graceful_failover flow (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/214); 2) Add a canary gate for healthcheck aggressiveness with traffic-weighted rollout and automated rollback based on acceptor_queue and streaming_error signals; 3) Enforce default SDK backoff policy via CI checks for internal services (SRE-3291); 4) Harden edge acceptor to better detect and clear half-open sockets sooner without triggering upstream resets; 5) Add a regression test in staging that simulates client burst + healthcheck flapping.
runbook_updates: 1) Add a new runbook section 'ephemeral-proxy healthcheck loop' with play actions: identify proxy group, scale down, extend acceptor drain, rollback healthcheck delta; 2) Expand runbook troubleshooting playbooks to include specific observability queries for healthcheck-fail-rate, tcp_rst_rate, acceptor_queue_length, and streaming_fragment_rate; 3) Add a prerequisite step to all proxy healthcheck changes that enforces a 5% canary for 30 minutes before group-wide rollout; 4) Document communication steps to reach partner teams for throttling test traffic.
action_items: SRE: ship proxy patch that avoids TCP RST for healthcheck failures (owner: Ravi, due: 2029-09-10)
Edge: implement automated canary gating for proxy config rollouts (owner: Chen, due: 2029-09-17)
SDK: revert override that disables exponential backoff in internal client libraries and add CI guardrails (owner: Marta, due: 2029-09-07)
Observability: add synthetic test that simulates healthcheck failure during a client burst and create dashboard (owner: Ethan, due: 2029-09-12)
Product: notify affected partners and add guidance for scheduled test jobs to avoid peak windows (owner: Aisha, due: 2029-09-06)
Runbook: add the 'ephemeral-proxy healthcheck loop' section and run the tabletop drill (owner: SRE-runbooks, due: 2029-09-20)
notes: Unusual aspects: this incident was triggered by a relatively small partner test burst. If the proxy healthcheck policy had a softer failure mode the incident would have likely been limited to a single proxy group. The interaction of multiple systems (proxy behavior, edge acceptor draining, client SDK backoff) created a cross-cutting failure mode. We should treat future proxy config changes as high-risk and require SRE sign-off for anything that alters connection handling or resets. Recommend a cross-team tabletop using this incident scenario.
postmortem_review: Scheduled: 2029-09-09 16:00 UTC. Attendees: SRE, Edge, Proxy, SDK, Product partner reps. Goals: review fixes, verify rollout gating, confirm timeline for action items. Decision record will be attached to SRE-3291 after review.
